newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to hold off cabinet reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to hold off cabinet reshuffle.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat made clear on Saturday that he would not take immediate action on an offer by most of his ministers to resign.

"This is still (a) long period (away)," Arafat said in English when asked if he would act on an offer by 16 of his 18 ministers to quit over allegations by legislators of corruption and mismanagement in the Palestinian Authority.

He spoke in Gaza on his return from Egypt where he had talks with President Hosni Mubarak about the grave crisis in the peace process with Israel following a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem on Wednesday.
The twin blasts killed 15 people, including the two attackers, prompting Israel to suspend peace contacts and initiate a security clampdown.
Cabinet ministers also said Arafat would not carry out a reshuffle soon despite the offer, made at a cabinet meeting on Friday night in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
"The President desires to postpone the issue for the time being because of the very difficult circumstances in the political process," Telecommunications Minister Imad al-Falouji told Reuters.
Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo, a close confidant of Arafat and one of the two ministers not to offer to resign, said the move by his colleagues was "meaningless".
"The people will discover soon that the ministers' move was meaningless, therefore I refuse to participate in theatrical steps of that kind," Abed Rabbo told Reuters.
Arafat has previously indicated that he is prepared to reshuffle his cabinet but Transport Minister Ali al-Qawasmeh said on Friday he doubted the Palestinian leader would act now.
"No resignation at this time...we must be united together in front of the Israeli measures," Qawasmeh, told Reuters on Friday night.
The Palestinian Legislative Council gave Arafat one month on Thursday to dissolve his cabinet, voting 56-1 that he appoint a new team of "qualified and experienced ministers".
Their overwhelming vote, which is non-binding, followed a report from a panel of nine legislators detailing instances of alleged corruption and squandering of funds.

Planning Minister Nabil Shaath, who was not at Friday's cabinet meting, also did not offer to resign. The legislators' panel this week recommended putting Shaath and Civilian Affairs Minister Jamil al-Tarifi on trial on suspicion of corruption and misuse of funds. Both men have denied any wrongdoing.

Evidence of apparent corruption and mismanagement by ministers and officials in the Palestinian Authority has deepened resentment and frustration among ordinary Palestinians coping with economic hardship.

It has embarrassed Arafat with international donors, including the European Union and the United States, who have disbursed $1.5 billion in aid since the PLO's interim peace deals with Israel in 1993.
